question: Shigella dysenteriae is the most common cause of bacillary dysentery in Indian children, and it causes disease by invading the colonic mucosa rather than by producing a secretory enterotoxin.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Shigella is the commonest cause of dysentery in Indian children. Its pathogenesis is INVASION — it penetrates and destroys colonic epithelial cells (unlike cholera, which is purely secretory). The small-volume, blood-stained, mucoid stool with tenesmus reflects this colonic mucosal destruction.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Shigella (especially S. dysenteriae type 1 and S. flexneri in India) invades the colonic epithelium directly, causing mucosal destruction, bleeding, and the characteristic small-volume bloody-mucoid stools with tenesmus. S. dysenteriae also produces Shiga toxin (Stx1), which can cause HUS as a complication. This mucosal invasion mechanism contrasts with V. cholerae (pure secretory, no invasion).
